metaDescription: Transfer switches matched to gasoline portable generators by size, from a 15A plug box to 30A and 50A circuit kits, with receptacle and sizing advice.
expertTake: The Nature's Generator 30A 6-circuit unit is the pick for the typical gasoline portable with a 30A outlet, because it fits the middle of the market and carries a UL listing in its title. The RVMATE 15A is the value pick for a small gas generator. Anyone with a 50A generator should move up to a 10 or 12 circuit kit and hire an electrician.
introParagraphs: Gasoline portable generators cover a huge range, from a small unit with a couple of household outlets to a large machine with a four-prong 50 amp receptacle. The transfer switch has to match what the generator can actually deliver, or one of the two parts will be wasted.

Start with the generator's outlet panel and its running watts, because the switch is chosen to fit those, not the other way around. After that, think about how many circuits you want, whether any are 240 volt, and where the inlet will live so the engine can run outdoors, safely away from the house.

products.name: Nature's Generator 30A 6-circuit 120V manual transfer switch
products.description:
Middle-of-the-market generators are the target, and this switch fits them. A 30 amp, 120 volt rating works out to about 3,600 watts, which is a realistic output for a typical gasoline portable with an L5-30 or similar outlet. UL listing is named in the title, and manual selector switches let you pick which of the six circuits ride on the generator.

Six circuits suit the usual essentials, such as the refrigerator, a freezer, a furnace blower, a few lights and a sump pump on 120V. It sits above the RVMATE for capacity and below the 50A kits for reach. Because it carries no 240V positions, a well pump or a dryer is out of scope, so the match is a generator whose owner has no 240V must-haves.

The real-world lesson with gasoline engines is fuel and exhaust. Store a fresh can outside, keep the generator on level ground away from the wall and run the engine for a few minutes each month. Exercise the selectors twice a year and tape a printed load list on the cover so the household can follow it. Add the order in which loads should come on, with the biggest motor first, because a generator that is loaded all at once will bog down and sometimes stall.
products.bestFor: Typical gasoline portables with about 3,600W at 120V and no 240V needs.
pros: 30A at 120V matches a typical portable's output
UL listing cited in the title
Six circuits cover a normal essentials list
Manual selectors give per-circuit control
cons: 120V only, so no well pump or dryer
Needs an electrician and likely a permit

products.name: RVMATE 15A 125V manual transfer switch with breaker

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Auxiliary power to a home circuit

products.description:
Small generators are the usual partner for a 15A box. At 125 volts, 15 amps is about 1,800 watts, a sensible match for a small gasoline unit or an inverter that powers one circuit. The listing cites ETL certification and a circuit breaker for manual switching, with a pre-drilled inlet box that makes mounting straightforward.

What it will not do is carry a household's worth of loads. Compared with the Nature's 30A, you give up four circuits and half the amperage, but you gain a plainer install and a lower tier. If your gasoline generator has a 30A outlet, this box leaves capacity unused, and the matching switch is the 30A model above.

For care, run the generator under load for a few minutes each season, check the inlet cover and press the breaker to confirm it moves freely. Pull the carburetor bowl fuel before long storage and keep a fuel stabilizer on hand, because a stale tank is what kills most gasoline portables in the first real outage. Running the carburetor dry before long storage, or shutting the fuel valve and letting the engine consume the bowl, avoids that gummed jet.
products.bestFor: Small gasoline generators feeding one household circuit.
pros: ETL certification cited in the listing
Breaker adds overload protection
Pre-drilled inlet box eases mounting
Low tier for a certified box
cons: About 1,800W ceiling is easy to outgrow

products.name: Afurkuot 20A 125V NEMA 5-20P transfer switch with breaker
products.description:
Twenty amps at 125 volts is about 2,500 watts, a figure that matches the 5-20 household outlets on most small gasoline generators. The listing cites ETL listing, a NEMA 5-20P inlet and a built-in breaker, with knockouts on four sides so conduit can enter from any direction.

Where it differs from the RVMATE is the extra 5 amps and the T-slot style 5-20 inlet, which accepts the cord most owners already carry for a job site or a camper. That makes it a sensible bridge between the 15A box and the 30A kit for a contractor-style generator with two 20A outlets. Next to the Nature's 30A, it controls one circuit rather than six.

Label the inlet and the cord, then practice the connection before the storm. Keep the box where the cord can reach the generator without stretching, and check the plug fit each season. A gasoline engine on a small frame is easy to move, so choose a permanent, shaded generator spot and mark it on the ground so the cord length always works.
products.bestFor: One 20A circuit fed from a contractor-style gasoline generator.
pros: 20A rating gives margin over 15A boxes
ETL listing cited in the listing
Built-in breaker protects the circuit
Knockouts on four sides for routing
cons: Enclosure is not stated as weather rated

products.name: DSGSANO 50A 10-circuit Pro/Tran2 style manual switch
products.description:
Fifty amps at 240 volts is about 12,000 watts, which is the neighborhood of the largest gasoline portables. The listing gives ten circuits and marks or tags on the wires to help sort them at install, and it supports up to ten circuits for power transfer. It also warns that you need some basic knowledge of electrical circuits.

That warning is worth taking seriously. A 50A kit is a project for an electrician, and the product data does not cite a safety listing, so ask the inspector before you buy. Against the Nature's 50A, it offers fewer slots but a lower price tier, and it follows a layout familiar to anyone who has seen a Pro/Tran style box.

Once installed, plan for a heavy cord and a generator with a matching four-prong receptacle. Gasoline generators this large burn a lot of fuel, so store extra safely and rotate it. Exercise the switches twice a year and keep the circuit list current as appliances change. A kit with this many positions is only as good as its labels, so spend an evening with a label maker after the electrician leaves.
products.bestFor: Large gasoline portables with a 50A outlet and a longer circuit list.
pros: 50A at 240V suits the biggest portables
Ten circuits cover a long list
Wires are marked to help with sorting
Lower price tier than the 12-circuit kit
cons: No approval mark is cited in the data

products.name: Nature's Generator 50A 12-circuit 120/240V transfer switch
products.description:
Reconfigurable slots are what set this switch apart. The listing explains that interchangeable positions let you set it up as twelve 120V circuits or six 240V circuits, so a mixed household can tune it to its own loads. The 50A, 120/240V rating and UL listing in the title point to a large gasoline generator with a 50A receptacle.

It has the most circuits of any pick here, so it fits a house with a long list of essentials. Compared with the DSGSANO, it offers two more slots and a stated UL listing, at a higher tier. Compared with the 30A model, it opens up 240V loads like a well pump.

Treat the configuration as a project record. Write down which positions are paired for 240V, keep the diagram with the generator manual and have an electrician review any change. Take a photo of the finished interior before the cover goes on, since that picture is the fastest way to explain the layout to a repair person years later. A gasoline generator of this size is heavy and loud, so plan a flat, ventilated spot and a cord long enough to keep it far from the house.
products.bestFor: Houses with a long essentials list and a 50A gasoline generator.
pros: Up to twelve circuits on a 50A switch
Configurable as twelve 120V or six 240V
UL listing cited in the title
Opens the door to 240V well pumps
cons: Highest install effort in the lineup

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 15A or 20A household outlet points to the RVMATE or Afurkuot, a 30A locking outlet points to the Nature's 30A, and a four-prong 50A receptacle points to the DSGSANO or Nature's 50A. The receptacle tells you the amp class before any spec sheet. Never adapt a 50A outlet down to a 30A inlet without a proper breaker. The adapter can leave the wiring protected only by the generator's much larger breaker, which will not trip until the wire is already overheating.

Gasoline generators advertise a big starting figure and a smaller running figure. The switch must be sized to the running watts, with the startup surge handled by the generator's capacity. A 15A box limits you to about 1,800W regardless of the engine.

The Nature's 30A offers six 120V circuits, the DSGSANO ten, and the Nature's 50A up to twelve or six at 240V. Count your must-run loads and note which need 240V, including the well pump or electric water heater that many buyers forget until the box is on the wall. A 120V-only box cannot run a well pump, and no setting on the generator changes that.
A switch does nothing without fuel. A mid-size gasoline generator may burn a few gallons a day, and a large one more. Store fuel outdoors in approved cans and rotate it with stabilizer.

Gasoline engines produce carbon monoxide, so the inlet position decides where the generator sits. Keep it outdoors and well away from windows and doors. A longer cord is a safer cord, within the gauge limits of the inlet, because the same distance that protects you from exhaust also keeps engine noise away from sleeping rooms.
The Nature's units cite UL listing in their titles, the RVMATE cites ETL, and the Afurkuot cites ETL, while the DSGSANO cites no mark in the data. Inspectors prefer listed gear. Ask before you buy.

specDecoder.meaning: The continuous power a generator can supply. Switches and wiring are sized to this number.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 15A box tops out near 1,800W and a 30A box near 3,600W at 120V.

specDecoder.meaning: A short surge figure that covers motor startup. It is not available continuously.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not size a switch to this number; the generator handles it.

specDecoder.meaning: A 240V circuit uses both hot legs and serves pumps and dryers. A 120V circuit uses one leg.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Nature's 50A can pair slots for 240V; the 30A Nature's cannot.

specDecoder.meaning: The plug shape on the generator panel. It tells you what cord and inlet fit.
specDecoder.watchFor: Match the inlet to the generator before ordering any of these kits.

specDecoder.meaning: A breaker inside the box trips on overload and protects the switch and wire. A reset button or lever restores it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The RVMATE and Afurkuot both include a breaker; the Nature's units rely on the panel's breakers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Generator class fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted the lineup by the generator size each switch suits, from small units to 12,000W portables. The ladder runs from the RVMATE 15A to the Nature's 50A. A mismatch wastes money or capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Circuit flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted circuits and voltage options. The Nature's 50A reconfigures between 120V and 240V, while the Nature's 30A stays at 120V. Flexibility helps a changing household.

howWeEvaluated.title: Approvals cited
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted UL, ETL or no mark in each listing, based on spec text and not lab work. Listed gear passes inspection more easily. Silent listings lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We estimated how much wiring each switch demands. A single-circuit unit like the Afurkuot is quick, a 10 or 12 circuit kit is a project. Labor shapes real cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for gasoline ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each switch fits a fuel-burning, noisy, exhaust-producing machine. Longer cords, outdoor inlets and clear labeling mattered. A switch that helps keep the engine outdoors scores well.

cards.label: Plug-in box
cards.text: The RVMATE and Afurkuot control one circuit and come mostly pre-wired. They are quick and cheap but cover only one load. They suit small gasoline generators.

cards.label: Circuit kit
cards.text: The Nature's 30A, DSGSANO and Nature's 50A bring six to twelve circuits into one box. They cover a full list but need rewiring at the panel. They suit mid and large generators.

howToChoose.note: Choose a plug-in box for one appliance and a circuit kit once the list passes three or four loads.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Plan fuel for several days, a long cord and a flat, ventilated generator spot. Pick a switch that lets you drop loads quickly when fuel runs low. Keep CO alarms working inside.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Nature's 30A six-circuit unit lets you shed a freezer or lights by flipping a selector. The Nature's 50A gives the most control on a big generator. A single plug-in box leaves no room to ration.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you rely on a well pump, a long essentials list or a 50A generator, which points to the Nature's 50A. Pay for a UL-listed box when an inspector is involved.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you protect one circuit from a small generator. The Afurkuot and RVMATE are the low-cost routes.

maintenance.why: A gasoline engine left idle gums its carburetor. A short loaded run keeps fuel moving and proves the switch.
Stale gasoline is the usual reason a portable fails to start. Stabilizer extends storage life.
Contacts and selectors that never move can stick. Cycle them with the generator off.
Cracked jackets and corroded pins are fire risks. Replace damaged cords.
Added freezers and pumps change the plan. A stale list invites overloads.

faq.q: What size transfer switch do I need for a gas generator?
faq.a: Match the switch to the generator's outlet and running watts. A 15A box suits about 1,800W, a 30A box about 3,600W at 120V, and a 50A kit the big portables. Choose the circuit count last.

faq.q: Can I use a 50A switch with a 30A generator?
faq.a: It works if the inlet and cord match the generator, but the generator limits the output, so the bigger switch adds cost without power. Match the switch to the outlet.

faq.q: Do I need a transfer switch if I just use extension cords?
faq.a: No. Plugging appliances straight into the generator avoids the house wiring. A switch is for feeding fixed circuits. Never backfeed through a wall outlet.

faq.q: How long can a gasoline generator run?
faq.a: It depends on the tank and load, often several hours on a tank at half load. Plan for refueling and keep extra fuel stored outdoors. Rest the engine as the manual advises.
Many jurisdictions expect listed equipment and some require a licensed electrician. The Nature's units cite UL and the RVMATE cites ETL. Ask your building department.

faq.q: Why does my generator trip when I switch circuits on?
faq.a: Motor loads draw a startup surge. Switch big loads on one at a time, starting with the largest. If trips continue, the generator may be undersized.
